summary: Robert A. F. Thurman (1941–2026) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying under Geshe Wangyal, Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, Gelek Rimpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as professor at Amherst College (1973–1988) and director at Columbia University (1988–2019).

Robert A. Orsi (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology who studied at Trinity College, Hartford, and Yale University. He held positions at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard (2001–2007), Northwestern (from ~2007), and Notre Dame (2020–2021).
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle, completing his degree by 2002.

Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under William Duguid Geddes at Aberdeen, and under Verrall, Reid, Shilleto, and Cowell at Cambridge, later serving at Cambridge as Lecturer in Sanskrit and Pembroke College Fellow.

Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. His appointments included research associate at the University of Chicago, research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (attested 1983).

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji under teachers including Suzuki, Blyth, and Senzaki, later serving at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1958–1969).

Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1999–2018), Tibet University (2000–2006), and both SOAS University of London and King's College London in ~2018.

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yatramulle Dhammarama, he worked as sub-librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor of Pali at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers (1737–1803) worked in Indology and law. Educated at Lincoln College, Oxford, he was a fellow at University College, Oxford, Vinerian Professor of English Law (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and Asiatic Society president (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) studied at Christ Church, Oxford, and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. Working in religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies, he served as Oxford's Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and All Souls College fellow (~1952–1974).

Robert Cummings Neville (born 1939) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who completed his studies at Yale University (~1960–1963). He held academic appointments at Yale (~1963–1965), Fordham University (~1965–1971), and Boston University (~1987).

Robert DeCaroli (born 1970), a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history, studied at UCLA under Robert L. Brown. He taught at UCLA and Loyola Marymount, and joined the faculty at George Mason University in ~2002.

Robert Deliège (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1978–1982). He held academic posts at the University of Kerala, Université catholique de Louvain (~1989), and KU Leuven (attested 2013).

Robert Duquenne is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held positions as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others, and under Kusan Sunim, before a long career at UCLA as professor (~1986–1992) and later Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology and art history. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he is attested in 2009 and as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History in 2026.

Robert E. Morrell is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held an academic post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies specialist. He studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983), holding adjunct appointments at Bastyr University, The Ayurvedic Institute, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert Epp (born 1926) is a scholar in the field of Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles, from ~1969 to 1972.
